papers.title: From a finite subgroup of $SO(3)$:$C_2$ leads to a Holant dichotomy
papers.abstract: Counting complexity within the Holant framework has been extensively studied through complexity dichotomy theorems. While substantial progress has been achieved for various restricted settings, the general complex-valued even-arity case without auxiliary unary signatures remains largely open. This paper studies a fundamental case in this program where the binary signatures induce a group structure satisfying \(M(B(\mathcal{F}))\cong C_2\). It is observed that projective equivalence classes of binary signature matrices naturally embed into finite subgroups of \(SO(3)\), providing an algebraic viewpoint for structural classification. This paper further identifies two fundamentally different regimes for the \(C_2\) case, namely the normal and isotropic cases, and analyzes their complexity behavior separately. Combining gadget constructions, decomposition techniques, interpolation arguments, and a realnumberization approach that transforms the complex-valued setting into an equivalent real-structured framework, this paper establishes a complete dichotomy theorem: for every even-arity signature set \(\mathcal{F}\) satisfying \(M(\B(\mathcal{F}))\cong C_2\), the problem \(\mathrm{Holant}(\mathcal{F})\) is either polynomial-time computable or \#P-hard. A Pauli-basis representation for signatures is further introduced as an algebraically natural language for organizing realizable signatures and revealing structural relations that are less transparent in the standard basis.

papers.title: Proper thinness at most 2: threshold and trivially perfect graphs
papers.abstract: The proper thinness of a graph is a parameter that generalizes proper interval graphs: the graphs of proper thinness 1 are exactly the proper interval graphs. The complexity of computing it is open even for cographs. In this paper we study it on two subclasses of cographs: threshold graphs and trivially perfect graphs. For threshold graphs, we show that the proper thinness is 1 if the graph is claw-free and 2 otherwise. For trivially perfect graphs, we characterize those of proper thinness at most 2 in three ways: structurally, through two properties of strongly consistent solutions that we call staggered and boundary; algorithmically, with a linear-time algorithm that decides whether the proper thinness is at most 2; and by forbidden induced subgraphs, showing that the $\mathrm{claw}_2$ and the lotus are exactly the minimal obstructions.

papers.title: Matroid Connectedness and Component Decomposition: Breaking the Quadratic Barrier
papers.abstract: Deciding whether a matroid is connected and computing its connected components are two fundamental algorithmic problems in matroid theory. Since the 1970s, the best known algorithms for both problems have used $O(n^2)$ independence queries on an $n$-element ground set. Our main contribution is to break this quadratic barrier: we give a deterministic algorithm that computes all connected components of a matroid on $n$ elements with $O(n \log{n})$ independence queries. Our algorithm for component decomposition combines fundamental basis exchanges with a disjoint-set union data structure, avoiding the explicit construction of the fundamental graph. Moreover, we show that our algorithm is asymptotically optimal by giving a lower bound based on a simple information-theoretic argument: any (deterministic or bounded-error randomized) algorithm to compute connected components needs $\Omega(n \log{n})$ independence queries. Then, we turn to the query complexity of deciding whether a matroid is connected. For this problem, we present an algorithm that uses $O(nh)$ independence queries, where $h \ge 1$ bounds the size of any chain of nonempty proper cyclic flats. The algorithm achieves asymptotically optimal linear query complexity on elementary split matroids, that include all paving matroids, and on arbitrary direct sums of uniform matroids.

papers.title: A (12/11+eps)-Approximation for Nonpreemptive Throughput Maximization
papers.abstract: We study unweighted nonpreemptive throughput maximization on an arbitrary number of identical machines: each job has a processing time and a release--deadline window, and the goal is to schedule as many jobs as possible. For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, we give a randomized $(12/11+\varepsilon)$-approximation. This improves the recent $(4/3+\varepsilon)$-approximation of Alexander Armbruster, Fabrizio Grandoni, Antoine Tinguely, and Andreas Wiese and the $(17/13+\varepsilon)$-approximation of Tong and Xu. For binary-encoded integral inputs, our algorithm runs in time $n^{O_\varepsilon(1)}\operatorname{poly}(N)$, where $N$ is the input length.

papers.title: Classification of Forbidden 0-1 Patterns by Their Extremal Function
papers.abstract: This paper concerns the maximum weight of $n\times n$ 0-1 matrices that avoid some pattern $P$, denoted $\operatorname{ex}(n,P)$. Furedi and Hajnal initiated a research program of classifying all patterns according to their extremal function, but to date, only the weight-4 patterns are completely understood. In this paper we make progress on several fronts of the classification problem. A pattern is light if its columns have weight 1 and linear if $\operatorname{ex}(n,P)=O(n)$. We characterize the set of weight-5 linear light patterns, and the set of weight-5 linear patterns more generally. Along the way we identify several new infinite classes of linear patterns, which support the Pettie-Tardos conjecture on characterizing all linear light patterns. It was known that there exist infinitely many minimally nonlinear patterns. We identify a specific infinite set of minimally nonlinear patterns. We also prove that there are $2^{\Omega(r)}$ weight-$r$ minimally nonlinear patterns, and that every minimally nonlinear pattern has extremal function $O(n\log n)$, with the exception of the 4-cycle. We classify many of the outstanding weight-5 patterns according to their extremal function, leaving only a small set remaining. The newly classified weight-5 patterns have extremal function $\Theta(n)$ or $\Theta(n\alpha(n))$. We also exhibit a large number of weight-6 patterns with extremal function $\Theta(n\log n/\log\log n)$, which is notable in that this function had not been encountered before for any single pattern $P$, though it was known to be the correct extremal function for a pair of forbidden patterns.

papers.title: An additive-square-free word over an alphabet of size 6
papers.abstract: An additive square over $\mathbb{N}$ is two consecutive nonempty blocks of the same length and same sum. For example, 1423 is an additive square, since 14 and 23 both have length 2 and sum 5. Solving a problem that has been open for more than 50 years, we give an example of an infinite word over a 6-letter subset of N that avoids additive squares.

papers.title: A combinatorial proof of a symmetric joint distribution on strict binary trees
papers.abstract: Nonplanar strict binary trees on $2n+1$ vertices are enumerated by the reduced tangent numbers $T_{2n+1}/2^n$, whose entries are refined by Poupard's triangle. Poupard defined the end of the minimal chain ($\mathrm{eoc}$) and the parent of the maximum leaf ($\mathrm{pom}$) on these trees, proving that $\mathrm{eoc}$ and $\mathrm{pom}+1$ share this triangular distribution. Foata and Han subsequently showed via tree calculus and partial difference equations that the joint distribution of $(\mathrm{eoc}, 2n+1-\mathrm{pom})$ is symmetric. By introducing an auxiliary tree statistic dual to $\mathrm{eoc}$, we give a bijective proof of this symmetry. Our proof composes a recursive bijection on strict binary trees, a bijection to alternating Andr\'e permutations, and the reverse-complement involution on permutations.

papers.title: Treewidth 3 in the Product Structure Theorem for Bounded Degree Graphs in Minor-Closed Classes
papers.abstract: We show that, for all positive integers $t$ and $\Delta$, there exists an integer $c$ such that, for every $K_t$-minor-free graph $G$ with maximum degree at most $\Delta$, there exists a graph $H$ of treewidth at most $3$ and a path $P$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of the strong product $H\boxtimes P\boxtimes K_c$. This improves on a previous result of Dujumovi\'c, Esperet, Micek, Walczak, and Wood (2022) by bounding the treewidth of $H$ independently of $t$ and $\Delta$. As an immediate consequence we obtain a bound of $O(r^4)$ on the $r$-weak colouring number of bounded-degree graphs from any proper minor-closed graph class.

papers.title: List packing for graphs with small arboricity
papers.abstract: We prove that every graph $G$ whose edge set is the union of $r$ forests has list packing number at most $2^r$. This means that for all $k\ge 2^r$ and every list-assignment $L$ with lists of size $k$, the graph $G$ admits $k$ disjoint proper $L$-colourings. While for large $r$ this bound is far from optimal, for $r\in\{1,2\}$ it is sharp. As a direct corollary of the case $r=2$, we obtain that every triangle-free planar graph has list packing number at most $4$, thus improving upon a result of Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Masa\v{r}\'ik, Mus\'ilek and Pangr\'ac and providing the optimal answer to a question of Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Postle and Norin on (weighted) $\epsilon$-flexibility of such graphs. As a corollary of the case $r=3$, we obtain a short alternative proof that every $K_5$-minor-free (and hence every planar) graph has list-packing number at most $8$, matching the state of the art. All results above also hold for the stronger notion of correspondence packing.

papers.title: Increasing arc-connectivity by bounded- and fixed-size inversions
papers.abstract: For a digraph $D$ and some $X \subseteq V(D)$, the inversion of $X$ is the operation of flipping all arcs both of whose endvertices are in $X$. We initiate the study of establishing arc-connectivity properties by applying inversions of bounded or fixed size. For fixed-size inversions, the feasibility problem is interesting. For all integers $p \geq 2$ and $k \geq 1$, we give a characterization of the digraphs that can be made $k$-arc-strong by applying inversions of size exactly $p$, provided they are sufficiently large. For bounded-size inversions, the feasibility problem is easy, so we focus on minimising the number of inversions. We prove that for all integers $p\geq 3$ and $k \geq 1$ and any $\epsilon>0$, there exists a polynomial-time $(4k-2+\epsilon)$-approximation algorithm for computing the minimum number of inversions of size at most $p$ that make a given digraph $k$-arc-strong. This is in stark contrast to other results on inversion optimization problems. On the other hand, we show that for any $p\geq 3$ and $k \geq 1$ the problem is NP-hard, and, moreover, APX-hard. As a result on parameterized complexity, we show that for any $k \geq 2$, it is $W[1]$-hard with respect to $p$ to decide whether a given digraph can be made $k$-arc-strong by applying a single inversion of size at most $p$. We also prove that for a given multidigraph, it is $W[1]$-hard with respect to $\ell$ to decide whether it can be made 2-arc-strong by applying $\ell$ inversions of size 2.

papers.title: $p$-ary (Non Weakly) Regular Bent Functions in Generalized $\cPS$ class
papers.abstract: We use $m$-dimensional partial spreads of $\fp^{2n}$, where $p$ is an odd prime, $n$ is a positive integer and $m$ divides $n$, to construct two classes of bent functions from $\fp^{2n}$ to $\fp$. Our construction generalizes the classes of $p$-ary $\cPS^{-}$ and $\cPS^{+}$ regular bent functions proposed by P. Lison\v ek and H. Y. Lu (Des. Codes Cryptogr. 73 (2014), 209--216). Unlike the original class, such bent functions can be either regular or non weakly regular.

papers.title: On Word Representations and Embeddings in Complex Matrices
papers.abstract: Embeddings of word structures into matrix semigroups provide a natural bridge between combinatorics on words and linear algebra. However, low-dimensional matrix semigroups impose strong structural restrictions on possible embeddings. Certain finitely generated groups admit faithful representations in SL(2, C) and other similar matrix groups. On the other hand, it is known that the product of two free semigroups on two generators cannot be embedded into the 2x2 complex matrices. In this paper we study embeddings of word structures into low-dimensional matrix semigroups over the complex numbers and develop new techniques for constructing word representations of the Euclidean Bianchi groups. These representations provide a symbolic framework and a natural first step towards analysing fundamental decision problems in 2x2 matrix semigroups.

papers.title: FPT Isomorphism Test for $F$-Free Tournaments
papers.abstract: We show that isomorphism of $F$-free tournaments can be solved in FPT time $f(k) \cdot n^{O(1)}$, where $k$ denotes the size of $F$, and $n$ denotes the size of the input tournaments. Our result extends on a previous FPT isomorphism test for tournaments of bounded twin-width [Grohe, Neuen 2024], as well as XP isomorphism tests parameterized by the VC dimension or the chromatic number [Ra{\ss}mann, Schweitzer 2026]. It also implies that every non-trivial hereditary class of tournaments admits a polynomial-time isomorphism test. Our algorithm builds on a combination of spectral, geometric, combinatorial and group-theoretic tools.

papers.title: Up or down at every integer: Collatz-type maps of arbitrary sets and the up-down graph
papers.abstract: For a set $S$ of positive integers let $T_S$ send $x$ to $\lceil 3x/2\rceil$ if $x\in S$ and to $\lceil x/2\rceil$ otherwise. The odd numbers give the Collatz map, the even numbers give it again after a shift by one, and $S=\mathbb{N}$ gives Mahler's map $x\mapsto\lceil 3x/2\rceil$. All these maps are subgraphs of the up-down graph $G$, in which every $x$ has the edges $x\to\lceil x/2\rceil$ and $x\to\lceil 3x/2\rceil$, and so are the families of maps in which the direction is forced at some numbers and free at the others. The cycles of the maps are the simple cycles of the subgraph, their divergent orbits are its rays, and all maps of a family are bounded exactly when the subgraph has no ray. We classify the simplest sets and show that density says little: some sets of density one send every orbit to 1, and some periodic sets of arbitrarily small density have increasing orbits. Every positive integer is the least element of a cycle of some map. The critical proportion of steps up is $\log_3 2$: cycles stay below it, divergent orbits stay above it, and both come arbitrarily close. For sets periodic modulo a power of 2, an effective up-frequency from a finite Markov chain takes the place of the density, and a finite computation can prove that every orbit reaches a cycle. Mahler's Z-number problem is implied by a question about one such map. Finally, we ask how far the Collatz map is from maps whose behaviour can be proved. Finite changes never help. Adding fewer than $\log_{3/2}N+1$ even numbers below $N$ makes an orbit increase, while removing the odd numbers congruent to 9 or 15 modulo 16, an eighth of all integers, gives a map all of whose orbits provably reach the cycle (1,2); removing 22 residue classes modulo 512, a proportion 0.043, also suffices.
